articles.title: Escape from New York Remake Loses Zack Snyder But John Carpenter Already Has a Backup Plan
articles.summary: It looks like it might be another L in the books for Zack Snyder. And while it's true that the movie he's potentially lost out on has been stuck in development hell for years, and that he was only attached back in June of this year, it can't feel great to no longer be associated […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google It looks like it might be another L in the books for Zack Snyder . And while it's true that the movie he's potentially lost out on has been stuck in development hell for years, and that he was only attached back in June of this year, it can't feel great to no longer be associated with the project—however that came about. The details are a little hazy, but it was initially reported by World of Reel that John Carpenter has said that Snyder is no longer on board for the Escape from New York remake and that he's been replaced by none other than Robert Rodriguez.

Snyder's involvement had been the only forward movement the project had seen in years, though it had previously had all sorts of names attached to it, including Radio Silence, Leigh Whannell, Brett Ratner, Len Wiseman, Breck Eisner, and Neil Cross. And when he sat down for an interview with Dropping Names , Carpenter, the original Escape from New York 's creator, revealed that Snyder was no longer involved, saying cryptically, "He’s not anymore, but he’s trying to get back. He’s trying to get back. We’ll see. Nice man. I liked him.” What exactly the filmmaker means by "he's trying to get back" is anyone's guess ( though surely some are hoping it's Snyderverse-related ).

It's still way too up in the air to know anything for sure, but some fans are definitely questioning why the production would swap out one director who finds himself on a losing streak for another on a seemingly worse streak. "I already saw a movie directed by Zack Snyder where people have to go into a cordoned-off zone for action hijinks. Somehow, even with a zombie tiger, it was f*cking tedious," said one fan about Snyder. As for Rodriguez, others were quick to add that he hasn't had a good film since Sin City , which he directed alongside Frank Miller.

Though some are skeptical about Snyder no longer being involved in the project, especially as this episode was shot months before its release. One listener said, "That’s not at all what was said on Dropping Names, and the episode was shot months ago. They specifically refer to Sam Neil being alive. In terms of the 'trying to get back' quote. That was about Snyder’s career, not this film. So, I’m sorry, we’re still stuck for now." And "stuck" is a great descriptor for how fans of the original (those who even want a remake) feel about Snyder as the prospective director. Overall, it's unclear what any of this really means, though it's worth noting that if Snyder isn't actually off the project, there's still Rodriguez waiting in the wings with an entirely different idea and script that Carpenter has reportedly signed off on.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Fans Disappointed After Nintendo Removes Entire Feature
articles.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake fans are dissapointed over a feature in the N64 original that was not carried forward to the new Nintendo Switch 2 remake. Other than some cut content here and there, the new Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is a very faithful remake of the original […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake fans are dissapointed over a feature in the N64 original that was not carried forward to the new Nintendo Switch 2 remake. Other than some cut content here and there, the new Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is a very faithful remake of the original game on N64. And you would expect it to be. When the game was re-released on GameCube, and then later remade on the 3DS, this was also the case, and it's the case because the N64 game is one of the best games ever made, in conversations with the likes of Red Dead Redemption 2 , various Grand Theft Auto games including the new GTA 6 , Half-Life 2 , BioShock , SoulCalibur, both Super Mario Galaxy games, fellow Zelda game Breath of the Wild , and a few others.

The new Nintendo Switch 2 remake is not a one-for-one remake, though. Not at all. Most of what has been changed has either gone largely unnoticed, or they are changes fans actually appreciate. This isn't the case with one change, though.

One of the top posts on the Ocarina of Time Reddit page this week is a post lamenting that the custom name save files of the original were not carried forward with the Nintendo Switch 2 remake. For those who didn't play the original game on the N64, when you started a new game, you were presented with a name-entry screen. You could put anything into this. And whatever you put became the name of Link. As a result, that name was substituted into dialogue. Obviously, players had fun with this.

The post above shot to the top of its respective Reddit page, so it is clearly a sentiment other fans of the Nintendo series share. If there was any doubt about this, the comments reinforce this.

"This is probably the only thing so far I don't like from the remake. It's probably due to the voices saying 'Link'."

Another comment adds, "A friend of mine once suggested I name him My Dude. I was confused at first, but trusted my friend and did as he asked. Link has had no other name since then."

What is lost on players who have come to The Legend of Zelda series in the modern era is that there was a time in the series where Link didn't have much distinction and personality, and was rather an avatar for the player. The character was iconic, but there was not much to him.

That said, the reason this was no doubt removed was because players could easily take advantage of it. Now, Nintendo could put restrictions in place, but then there would be blowback about that, and players would probably find a way around these restrictions. Further, some of the aforementioned removed content are the Super Mario easter eggs, which Nintendo removed because they want the game to be more immersive and mature. This same line of thinking would no doubt apply here as well. Maybe this feature will return in the leaked DLC , but it's highly unlikely.

articles.title: I’m In My Feelings Over The Chat Alfonso Ribeiro Had With Harry Shum Jr. And Jenna Johnson After Their DWTS Elimination
articles.summary: I'm emotional all over again.
articles.content:
The final weeks of Dancing with the Stars always feature really tough eliminations. However, the last few on the 2026 TV schedule have been brutal. Specifically, Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson went home during the semifinals after getting perfect scores for their Paso Doble and Glee- themed Quickstep . Now, co-host Alfonso Ribeiro has opened up about the conversation he had with the pair following their shocking elimination, and I'm feeling emotional all over again.

I’m also saddened for them. While Harry and Jenna always had some of the best routines of every episode, their DWTS journey was plagued by some controversy and intense online discourse. Of course, there was liftgate , which led to a comment from Johnson’s husband and fellow pro Val Chmerkovskiy that got him suspended from the show for a week. There was also the ongoing debate regarding the amount of dance experience Harry Shum Jr. had before doing DWTS .

It does feel like the mirrorball trophy could be anyone's. They’re all pretty good, and it’s clear that everyone left has a very devoted fan base. So, it’s unclear who will win, and an argument can be made for any of them. I mean, when I think about all this, there’s part of me that wants Amber Glenn to win , and thinks she can do it based on her scores and consistency. Meanwhile, Connor Wood’s social media likes prove he has a very devoted group of fans behind him that could help make up for his lower scores and push him across the finish line. Seriously, it’s anyone’s game.

I totally see his point. DWTS is a massive time commitment, and it’s an intense experience both physically and mentally. These stars put their everything into it, and so it’s sad to see any of them not reach the end.

articles.title: I Thought People Would Recognize Andrew Scott From Sherlock, But Another Role Comes Up Way More
articles.summary: His appeal goes far beyond Baker Street.
articles.content:
There's no denying Andrew Scott delivered one of the most compelling portrayals of Moriarty opposite Benedict Cumberbatch in what remains one of the standout adaptations of Sherlock Holmes . The show ran on the BBC for 4 seasons, and fans are still holding out hope for a 5th run . I honestly thought this would be the role he was most recognized for, but it turns out that's not the case. Without hesitation, Scott told me it's actually the “Hot Priest” from Fleabag .

I'm glad to see I'm not alone in this. For me, and clearly for a lot more people than I thought, Scott is the ‘Hot Priest.' He takes a man of the cloth and makes him layered, complicated, charismatic, and, above all, very sexy. If you've seen Fleabag , I'm sure the line “Kneel. Just kneel.” is burned into your brain for all eternity, just like it is mine. He clearly has a knack for making even a single line stick with audiences, as is the case with his one line in Saving Private Ryan .

Piper is spot on. I watched it, and there is no other word to describe that scene. But Scott is so much more than "hot." He is, in my opinion, a once-in-a-generation talent, and the roles he plays are memorable. He has this rare ability to make even the biggest performances feel incredibly personal, almost like he's speaking directly to each individual person watching. That's especially true in Elsinore . I think he's going to give Robert Pattinson a run for his money this Oscar season . Honest.

articles.title: Skydance Already Has the Perfect Script to Relaunch the Justice League, And It Almost Happened 20 Years Ago
articles.summary: Skydance wants to get the Justice League back in theaters, and the studio may already have the right script sitting in a drawer somewhere. With James Gunn and Peter Safran departing as DC Studios executives, incoming studio chief Jeremy Latcham has reportedly been tasked with getting DC’s biggest superheroes together as soon as he can. […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Skydance wants to get the Justice League back in theaters, and the studio may already have the right script sitting in a drawer somewhere. With James Gunn and Peter Safran departing as DC Studios executives, incoming studio chief Jeremy Latcham has reportedly been tasked with getting DC’s biggest superheroes together as soon as he can. Rather than start from scratch, Skydance could dust off a movie that almost got made 20 years ago.

Before Zack Snyder brought DC's biggest heroes together in 2017, Mad Max: Fury Road director George Miller almost made Justice League: Mortal . Warner Bros. pulled the plug when the movie was fully cast and deep into preproduction. Its completed screenplay eventually leaked online , revealing an ambitious superhero movie that might work even better today.

In 2007, Warner Bros. hired Miller to direct Justice League: Mortal from a screenplay by Kieran and Michele Mulroney. Unlike the Marvel Cinematic Universe, which spent years introducing its heroes before bringing the Avengers together, Miller’s film would have dropped viewers into a world where DC’s superheroes were already up and running. No backstory required.

The cast featured D.J. Cotrona as Superman and Adam Brody as the Flash, who would later reunite as members of the Shazam family, playing the adult superhero versions of Pedro Peña and Freddy Freeman, respectively. Common was cast as Green Lantern John Stewart. His imposing performance as Robert Sims in Silo offers a taste of what we missed. Miller later cast his Wonder Woman, Megan Gale, as the Valkyrie in Mad Max: Fury Road . Santiago Cabrera, originally cast as Aquaman , went on to star in Star Trek: Picard , while Hugh Keays-Byrne, cast as Martian Manhunter, played Immortan Joe in Fury Road . Jay Baruchel was set to play Maxwell Lord, with Teresa Palmer as Talia al Ghul. Palmer may be the only casting choice that truly needs to be corrected. A French Talia? Of course. But an Australian Talia al Ghul? I don't know, mate.

The 2007 writers' strike, as well as issues with Australian production incentives, derailed the film. Miller went on to create Fury Road , but Justice League: Mortal left a screenplay worth revisiting. Armie Hammer, who was prepared to take on the role of Batman. Below you can see some of the concept art and storyboards from the film, plus Kevin Smith talking to Hammer about almost starring in Miller’s movie.

Adapting the Tower of Babel Arc From JLA Ra's al Ghul uses Batman's contingency plans against the League in Mark Waid and Howard Porter's JLA: Tower of Babel . Mortal combines that premise with the events leading up to Infinite Crisis . Maxwell Lord hijacks Batman's Brother Eye surveillance system and uses his telepathic abilities to turn Superman against his teammates. The screenplay also puts a twist on one of the most controversial moments from that era of DC Comics, when Wonder Woman snaps Lord's neck to free Superman from his control. That moment occurred in Wonder Woman #219, the conclusion of the four-part Superman: Sacrifice crossover. In Mortal , however, it's Batman who snaps Lord's neck.

Zack Snyder would later echo the comic book moment in Man of Steel , with Superman snapping General Zod's neck to save innocent lives. James Gunn famously detested this villainous version of Lord . Given the uncertainty surrounding Sean Gunn's future in the role, Skydance could revisit the darker interpretation introduced in Countdown to Infinite Crisis .

From David S. Goyer and Justin Marks' Green Arrow: Escape from Super Max to George Miller's Justice League: Mortal , Skydance has an abundance of abandoned DC projects it could revisit before commissioning new ones. Super Max would have seen Oliver Queen stripped of his identity and imprisoned alongside some of the DC Universe's most notorious supervillains.

Guillermo del Toro completed a screenplay for Justice League Dark that would have seen John Constantine assemble a team including Swamp Thing, Zatanna, and Deadman. Del Toro even envisioned frequent collaborator Doug Jones as Deadman . Following the success of Frankenstein , why not give the director another crack at DC's supernatural characters?

Ava DuVernay and comic book writer Tom King were also developing a film around Jack Kirby's New Gods. King has since returned to Kirby's Fourth World as the showrunner of Mister Miracle , an animated series starring Josh Hutcherson and Mackenzie Davis as Scott Free and Big Barda. The series is still in production, and it's entirely possible that some of the ideas King explored with DuVernay have found their way into the animated series. Skydance could build on that work with a live-action New Gods movie.

Skydance has not yet said what its future plans are for the DC Universe. But if Man of Tomorrow leaves the studio with a Justice League worth keeping, then Justice League: Mortal provides the perfect opportunity to tear it apart. What abandoned DC project would you like to see resuscitated by Skydance? Let us know in the comments below.

articles.title: Yu Yu Hakusho Needs a Modern Anime Revival for One Main Reason
articles.summary: Shueisha / Pierrot In recent years, there's been a massive uptick in classic anime series receiving new-and-improved reboots that aim to deliver modern animation, stories that stay more closely aligned to the story's original source material, and even new vocal performances from legacy cast members. These successful reboots, which include the likes of Ranma 1/2 and Urusei Yatsura, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google In recent years, there's been a massive uptick in classic anime series receiving new-and-improved reboots that aim to deliver modern animation , stories that stay more closely aligned to the story's original source material, and even new vocal performances from legacy cast members. These successful reboots, which include the likes of Ranma 1/2 and Urusei Yatsura , are introducing an old-school style of anime to new-age fans looking to sink their teeth into a wider variety of storytelling. One of the more popular classics that's yet to receive a proper re-adaptation is Yu Yu Hakusho , originally created by Hunter x Hunter 's mangaka Yoshihiro Togashi. Yu Yu Hakusho 's original anime adaptation from Studio Pierrot ran for 112 episodes beginning in 1992, and despite how iconic the series is, desperately deserves a fresh adaptation.

Yu Yu Hakusho follows Yusuke Urameshi, a 14-year-old delinquent who dies saving a young boy from a car accident. After being sent to the afterlife and proving his worth, Yusuke is given the chance to return back to the world of the living to work as a Spirit Detective who investigates paranormal threats and demons threatening to harm normal humans. Contrasting from other anime released during the same era, Yu Yu Hakusho stayed surprisingly close to the source material, however, the series did cut some of the manga's earlier chapters short and expanded upon other story arcs with some additional content not present in Togashi's original work. While there's nothing inherently wrong with the original adaptation of Yu Yu Haksuho , the series could benefit greatly from getting a high quality reboot.

With the anime community's rapid growth spurt over the last decade, new anime fans are clamoring season-to-season to find new shows to latch onto. While there have been plenty of great new ideas hitting these lineups, seeing beloved classics return with modernized animation techniques and production teams have given a number of old-school series a fresh audience to bring them back to life . Yu Yu Hakusho is the perfect show for audiences right now; the series' focuses on themes of personal growth intertwined with the emotional and psychological cost of violence within a supernatural conflict between humans and demons.

These kinds of stories have been deeply resonating with anime fans — with similar shows like Jujutsu Kaisen becoming some of the biggest pop culture phenomenons on the planet. One of the bigger questions surrounding a re-adaptation of Yu Yu Haksuho would be what studio and directors would be capable of pulling off such a large scale project . If fans were to receive a complete remake that adapted all 19-volumes of Togashi's original work, the show would need a production studio capable of taking on longterm productions without fear of quality dips or production stalls.

While MAPPA is a fan-favorite dream studio for imagining projects like this, other popular studios like Studio Bones, which has handled long-form shonen series like My Hero Academia and Mob Psycho 100 , or even Wit Studio, who made a name for themselves with their adaptations of Vinland Saga , Spy x Family , and Attack on Titan stand out as possible choices. That said, Yu Yu Hakusho may find a better home with Madhouse — known for their stunning adaptation of Frieren: Beyond Journey's End , and perhaps in this particular case, for their work on 2011's adaptation of Hunter x Hunter .

Yu Yu Hakusho wouldn't be the first of Togashi's manga to receive a reboot that makes a cultural statement for anime fans. The 2011 reboot of Togashi's Hunter x Hunter stole anime fans from that decade and beyond's hearts , and for good reason. The Madhouse-produced series had a 148-episode run that spanned three years, and beautifully translated Togashi's signature illustrations to animation. Not to mention, Hunter x Hunter 's 2011 reboot only helped in skyrocketing the popularity of the original work more, which now has well over 100-million copies in circulation, making it one of only around twenty-five other series to reach the same level of acclaim.

While Yu Yu Hakusho is an incredible series by its own merit, having 19-collected volumes after running in Weekly Shonen Jump magazine for four years . Even years after the series came to an end, the manga reportedly has 78-million copies in circulation. Yu Yu Hakusho has consistently ranked in popularity polls around the globe like Nielsen BookScan in North America, with multiple volumes from the series ranking week-to-week. In Japan alone, Yu Yu Hakusho earned the Shogakukan Manga Award in 1993's shonen category and ranked 17th in 2021's TV Asahi's Manga Sosenkyo poll wherein 150,000 manga readers voted on their top 100 series.

Needless to say, a high quality, action-packed reboot of Yu Yu Hakusho would immediately grab the attention of thousands of anime fans around the globe and dominate the anime community. Would you want to see a new version of Yu Yu Hakusho ? Let us know your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: ‘Blade’ Director Says ‘Sinners’ Was “So Much Bolder” Than What Marvel Was Attempting & “Life’s Too Short To Make Sh*t Films”
articles.summary: If you thought “ Blade ”-gate had died down and director Bassam Tariq had already said his piece about Marvel’ s troubled reboot, guess again. The filmmaker, originally hired to direct “Blade” with Mahershala Ali in the title role, opened up again about his frustrating experience at Marvel Studios, revealing that the production began casting actors without a proper screenplay. The experience ultimately taught him a valuable lesson: “Life’s too short to make shit films.” Speaking in a new interview with The New Arab, Tariq offered an unusually candid account of his Marvel experience, perhaps speaking more freely given the relatively low-profile outlet, as he described the strange circumstances of developing a major studio production without a finished screenplay. Whether the starlet is out and about or not, though, her music consistently plays across the airwaves. So what's it like for Grande to hear her work in public? Well, the Wicked actress got real about the wildest place she heard her music, and believe me when I say I was not expecting her to mention a bikini wax while explaining.

With the former Nickelodeon actress being one of the best-selling artists of all time and having ten Billboard Top 100 singles, she gets a lot of airtime. So it's pretty much a given that Grande would hear her own music now and then. As a matter of fact, when Harper’s Bazaar asked Grande about the wildest place she ever heard her own songs, she mentioned a wax:

Yeah, I was one time getting a bikini wax. And the song came on, and I didn’t think [the bikini wax employee] knew who I was at all. I never assume that anyone does.

Grande continued to mimic the satisfied look of the wax specialist, who also said to her, “And my kids love your show!” While the former child has spoken before about how fame tends to complicate her music career , it looks like it can also come with some surreal and somewhat funny encounters with fans as well.

A celebrity like Hugh Jackman can relate to the joy of hearing his own music in public. Months after his movie, The Greatest Showman, premiered, he recalled overhearing the film’s soundtrack as he was making his way to the door of an apartment or hotel. I can imagine it feeling like such an honor for an artist when someone is enjoying their work in some form or another.

Let's also be real, as Ariana Grande ’s music is easy to love, given her immense talent. Per a fun fact about Grande , five-time Grammy winner Gloria Estefan spotted her talent when she was 8 years old and singing on a cruise ship. I think it's fair to say Estefan knows talent when she sees it.

And, this year, the “Positions” singer’s Eternal Sunshine Tour was her second highest-grossing tour she’s had, earning $107.9 million.

Now, on the heels of that top-selling tour ended in, Grande can celebrate her role in the highly anticipated Focker-In-Law . The film sees Grande play the fiancée of Greg Focker’s son, who also ends up having a rivalry with her future father-in-law. It’ll be exciting to see “The Way” singer go back to her comedy roots and mix it up with stars like Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro .

I wonder whether Grande's music was played on set and if so, which tracks were selected. Personally, I think a set seems like a more obvious place for her to hear her songs as opposed to a place where she can get a bikini wax. That aside, check out the Oscar nominee in Focker-in-Law when it opens on November 25th amid the 2026 movie release .

articles.summary: Despite Marvel Studios' best efforts to keep almost everything about the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday completely under wraps, it seems that one actor might not have gotten the memo, accidentally spilling the exact release date of when the next trailer will be releasing. While signing autographs, Haley Atwell, who plays Peggy Carter, spilled the beans, saying […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Despite Marvel Studios' best efforts to keep almost everything about the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday completely under wraps , it seems that one actor might not have gotten the memo, accidentally spilling the exact release date of when the next trailer will be releasing. While signing autographs, Haley Atwell, who plays Peggy Carter, spilled the beans, saying that there would be a new trailer for Doomsday dropping on Monday —which means that we're only two days away from (hopefully) unrecycled content, and that's enough to get anyone excited.

While signing autographs after the Broadway premiere of Much Ado About Nothing , Atwell stunned fans, saying, "There's a new trailer, I think, dropping on Monday." She stopped herself, adding, "Am I allowed to have said that?" But when one fan asked if it was a " thumbs up or a thumbs down ," she said, "I watched the trailer. I was like, 'This is amazing.'" And when that same fan mentioned that they heard the trailer contained some sad moments that might just leave the audience in tears, the actor replied, "There's going to be some feelings."

Hayley, "There's a new trailer I think, dropping on Monday. I watched the trailer. I was like, this is amazing." Fan: "I heard very sad though. We're going to all cry." Hayley, "There's going to be some feelings." Via. cginolfi23 🗓20th November 2026 stage door. #HayleyAtwell pic.twitter.com/6TxzspanAT

When one fan begged to know that this wasn't old footage, another saved the day, saying, "Stage Door at Much Ado About Nothing on Broadway, which opened Thursday night. We won." It's also led some fans to theorize that the trailer will drop during Monday Night Football. It's worth noting that everyone also thought that the Super Bowl would have a Doomsday trailer, and that everyone was subsequently disappointed when that didn't happen. So when exactly during the day that the trailer will drop is still anyone's guess, but there are potentially a few options.

When discussing previous trailers and their release timelines, one fan said, "Previous Avengers films received an official trailer a month or so prior to their release. I’m not clamoring for another full trailer, but I’d love to see one, especially since the other trailers haven’t really blown me away. The film still carries an atmosphere of 'unearned amalgamation of characters from many years of films.'" And that's certainly a sentiment that's been making the rounds among the fandom, with fans lamenting the way that Marvel Studios has handled the film's marketing up to this point, with Visa ads, MLB TV spots that rehash old content, and the Russos even appearing as their own special guests at random events.

And while some fans are accusing others of ingesting mass amounts of copium, claiming that we're really only in for more of the same few scenes we've already seen, the general hope is certainly that Atwell is right not only about the trailer dropping, but that it's as incredible as she claims, and that Kevin Feige won't feel too contrary about the news being leaked, deciding instead to move the trailer release date to keep fans on their toes.

Unlike Sony's recent theatrical release of The Social Reckoning , which arguably didn't resonate with the current tech era we're living in, Neon is unwrapping Luca Guadagnino 's Artificial about Open AI co-founders Sam Altman, Ilya Sutskever and Elon Musk at a time when we fear the technology will end us.

Now whether that's in regards to our existence or our financial livelihoods is another question.

Earlier this week, former OpenAI alum and Altman rival Dario Amodei's Anthropic went public creating a $1.18 trillion company. However, shares fell from its $111 day-of-market price to $88.91 EOD Friday. Neon is shrewdly opening Artificial limited on Christmas Day (the perfect time to launch a sophisticated adult skewing awards contender), and in the run-up to that release, following premieres at New York Film Festival and BFI London Film Fest, along with current awards voter screenings, anticipation is boiling for the pic evident in its current 95% fresh Rotten Tomatoes critics rating. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories News Timothée Chalamet Addresses Possibility Of A 'Call Me by Your Name' Sequel: "Never Say Never" News Sam Altman On 'Artificial' Movie About Him -- Not Among "Ten Weirdest Things In My Life" Right Now

As a filmmaker who knows something about love with the Zendaya starring tennis love triangle pic, Challengers , and Oscar winning gay romance, Call Me By Your Name, we spoke with Guadagnino on the latest Crew Call as to what pulled him into the OpenAI-verse. Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

Take a listen below. Essentially, it's about about a bunch of young mad, narcissistic scientists acting like flawed Greek Gods in San Francisco:

Well before its theatrical release, Artificial generated a lot of controversy as its original studio, Amazon MGM Studios, backed away from the movie out of fear of OpenAI. That's because Amazon has a $50 billion investment in the Altman non-profit.

However, unlike the Facebook camp back when Social Network was getting released in 2010, there's been zero ill will coming from Altman or OpenAI about Guadaganino's film. In fact, you could say they're great sports. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

In a sit-down with the Vanity Fair podcast, Altman says he "did not" coerce Amazon to drop Artificial. "I don't know anyone else who did," he added, "I didn't speak to Jeff Bezos."

In fact, Guadagnino brazenly shot the pic outside Altman's house in San Francisco. The filmmaker tells us about that. For Altman, he was giddy about running into his onscreen doppelgänger, Andrew Garfield: "One morning, I was walking down the street to get coffee and there were all these cameras and there was a guy dressed exactly like me with the same backpack, walking so much, I felt like I was in a weird glitch or a simulation."

Altman emphasized to Vanity Fair that Garfield "did walk like me."

While Altman hasn't seen Artificial, his reaction to the trailer is, "I don't think they're going for accuracy, so in that sense it doesn't bother me. They're trying to make a good movie and maybe it will be good. It won't be good as an accurate depiction, except for the walk. I'm sure they'll get other parts right at least accidentally."

One of the jaw dropping moments shown in the Artificial trailer is Altman having a bunker in his wine country estate loaded with guns.

"That is an example of an inaccuracy," Altman told Vanity Fair, "There's no bunker with firearms on the wall."

"I have a survivalist mindset," Altman admitted, "but I don't have a setup that is depicted in that trailer."

Guadagnino tells Deadline, "I have validated the validating information that has been vetted: He does have guns."

While the filmmaker experienced zero pushback from OpenAI and Altman during production on the Simon Rich script, he says "We were very careful that everything that was in the movie had to be approved legally, so that we were not bending facts and reality for our narrative purposes. But, because the truth in this case is more extraordinary than any fiction, that was okay. Because we had the drama, we had the juice."

When it came to Amazon exiting Artificial , Guadagnino had a Zen mindset: "I was cool because I like disruptions, very much."

"Their decision to give the movie to us to find another home was truly honorable, because they could have written off the movie and (said) 'Bye-bye'."

As far as Artificial being a hot potato that no studio wanted to handle, except NEON, Guadagnino asserts that "All the speculation about nobody wanting the movie; I like to think that there was the need (by the media) to fill blank pages with nothing."

For off the bat, per Guadagnino, NEON was first, front and center in their passion to takeover the project after CAA screened it for them. Listen above for more details.

When it comes to the paranoia out there that AI is the catalyst for human extinction in ten years, the filmmaker tells Deadline, "I don't have trust and I don't have faith in humans."

His suspicions about AI stem from growing up during the Cold War. "I remember very well in 1985 when Chernobyl happened," he adds.

And there's myriad reasons for concerns about AI, from a Chatbot being at the center of 16-year old Adam Raine's suicide , to AI trespassing and impostering another company's security space

We also talk with the Call Me By Your Name Best Picture Oscar nominee on why Andrew Garfield was the right guy to play Altman, and the Open AI Boss' sincerity when it comes to creating guardrails for the technology.

articles.title: 3 More '90s Animated Shows That Deserve Modern Reboots, And All Had Incredible Toy Lines
articles.summary: The 1990s were something of a golden age for animated television, and the decade is fondly remembered by those who grew up on a steady diet of colorful Saturday morning cartoons about colorful superheroes, anthropomorphic animals, and action-packed adventures. It was an era in which many cartoons had their own toy lines, as several networks […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The 1990s were something of a golden age for animated television, and the decade is fondly remembered by those who grew up on a steady diet of colorful Saturday morning cartoons about colorful superheroes, anthropomorphic animals, and action-packed adventures. It was an era in which many cartoons had their own toy lines , as several networks and studios developed entire franchises around the idea of delivering tie-in action figures and playsets that would appeal to their young audiences. Some of the era's most popular cartoons have gone on to secure recent success through modern reboots and big-screen adaptations, while others have sadly become pretty obscure.

With so many modern reboots finding success with both nostalgic audiences and newcomers who missed out the first time around, there are plenty more candidates that deserve to be rescued from obscurity. With advances in animation technology, rebooting the following shows now seems easier than ever, and the '90s kids that loved these cartoons the first time around are sure to get excited about an updated version. While they might not be the best known to modern audiences, the following animated shows could all easily appeal if they were simply given a modern facelift.

When it comes to great animated shows from the 1990s that don't get enough love, SWAT Kats: The Radical Squadron is something of a gold standard. It followed the adventures of two anthropomorphic cats named T-Bone and Razor as they operate as vigilantes, protecting their home, Megakat City, from an array of supervillains. Combining high-flying aerial combat with an assortment of gadgets and vehicles, SWAT Kats proved hugely popular with kids in the mid-'90s, as did its tie-in line of action figures.

The good news is that a SWAT Kats revival is already in the works. First announced in 2022, the original show's creators, Christian and Yvon Tremblay, are already working to bring its characters back to our screens, delivering SWAT Kats action to a whole new generation. It's not hard to understand why the revival is a good idea, as the superhero-style narrative is likely to be more popular than ever, and the added nostalgia factor, combined with the increased capabilities of modern animation, seems to be a recipe for surefire success. Though concrete details on the revival are currently scarce, it's a reboot that will hopefully bring the beloved but forgotten '90s cartoon back to life to achieve even greater success.

The name Mighty Max is one that is surprisingly evocative for '90s kids, especially as those who didn't grow up during that decade aren't likely to recognize it at all. First established as an incredibly inventive series of miniature playsets, Mighty Max then made the jump to the small screen with its own TV show in 1993. It followed the adventures of a young boy named Max who discovers a magic baseball cap capable of transporting across time and space. The original toy line might have been more widely successful and memorable, but the corresponding series is an underrated '90s gem.

Considering the huge scope of Mighty Max 's premise, it's easy to see how a modern reboot could work. Not only does it provide the opportunity for a great animated fantasy show , but also for another line of tie-in toys that could help define the childhoods of a whole new generation. Exploring Max's story all over again using modern animation techniques could be a massive success with viewers of all ages, and that's without even mentioning how much those old playsets several of us still have gathering dust would appreciate in value.

Of all the great cartoons of the 1990s , Bucky O'Hare and the Toad Wars! stands out as one of the most criminally short-lived. Perhaps one of the most unique cartoons of the era — and that's really saying something, considering some of the weird shows that graced our screens back then — Bucky O'Hare followed a green rabbit and his ragtag crew of freedom fighters as they fought against the tyrannical Toad Empire against the backdrop of a large-scale intergalactic conflict. Despite only lasting for 13 episodes, Bucky O'Hare was another show that had an impressive accompanying Hasbro toy line.

A modern Bucky O'Hare reboot could capitalize on new animation technology to better explore the sprawling sci-fi ideas of the '90s show. The sense of adventure it captured even in its short run was timeless, and a revival could capitalize on the success of other animated shows in delivering high-concept sci-fi stories that appeal to all ages. If handled carefully, a Bucky O'Hare reboot for modern audiences could achieve the success the original was robbed of, making full use of the imaginative premise it never got the chance to explore.

articles.summary: Rockstar Games' next game after GTA 6 has potentially leaked, and it's not GTA 7 or Red Dead Redemption 3. And unfortunately, it's not Bully 2, for the Bully fans who have been desperate for a sequel for two decades. These would be the three most obvious candidates, particularly the first two. According to a […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Rockstar Games' next game after GTA 6 has potentially leaked, and it's not GTA 7 or Red Dead Redemption 3 . And unfortunately, it's not Bully 2 , for the Bully fans who have been desperate for a sequel for two decades. These would be the three most obvious candidates, particularly the first two. According to a new leak, though, Rockstar Games is taking a break from Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption . Given both print money and both are some of the most critically-acclaimed pieces of entertainment in entertainment history, it's hard to imagine this being the case, but it apparently is.

Back in September, we relayed word of an interesting report from an anonymous leaker who revealed not only what Rockstar Games next game was, but leaked many details on GTA 6 , including information about its endings. And the details ended up being accurate, which has fans of Rockstar Games re-examining what else the leaker said. And what else the leaker said was that the next game releasing from Rockstar Games is a sequel to L.A. Noire .

According to this leak, this sequel is going to take the series to San Francisco, and have players hunting down the infamous Zodiac Killer, a 1960s serial killer who has famously never caught. The leaker also notes that the game is targeting a 2030 release, so it is seemingly already an appreciable way into development. The leaker also notes that the game is set to put a large emphasis face scanning technology, and is specifically aiming to set a new industry standard in this regard. This would make sense, as this is exactly what the first game did back when it released in 2011. And it also makes sense because the core mechanic of the one-game series is interrogations.

For those unfamiliar with L.A. Noire , it is an action-adventure game released in 2011. It was published by Rockstar Games, but not developed by it. The developer was Team Bondi, which closed the same year the game released. It wasn't because the game wasn't successful, though. Upon release, it earned an 89 on Metacritic, and as of 2017, it had sold over 7.5 million copies. The same year, a slice of the game was made into a VR game and released as L.A. Noire: The VR Case Files . The series has been dormant ever since.

In terms of IP signifgance, Bully is probably the developer's third biggest IP, but it's a harder IP to revive, especially in the current social media climate. That said, it would be surprising to see L.A. Noire revived, unless it is contracted out, simply because Red Dead Redemption and Grand Theft Auto make too much money for them to have their releases pushed back for a new L.A. Noire game. To this end, take everythign above with a grain of salt.

articles.title: That Big Death In The End Of Oak Street Almost Went Down Very Differently
articles.summary: It was almost so much sadder.
articles.content:
SPOILERS AHEAD for The End of Oak Street , now streaming with a HBO Max subscription .

The End of Oak Street feels like one of those rare family-oriented sci-fi flicks we don’t see enough anymore. So, I was very surprised when Ewan McGregor ’s character dies in front of his wife and kids. It was completely heartbreaking to watch – especially right after that kinky dino scene . It really darkened the tone of the whole movie. But, as it turns out, it was originally even darker . Crazy, right? As Anne Hathaway revealed to Entertainment Weekly :

Now, I didn’t think Greg was going to come back when I watched the movie, because how could he? Once what’s left of the Platt family goes through the portal and realises they’ve travelled back in time, I was so happy with what happened next. Denise calls her husband to deliver a pizza, and he does just in time to be outside the radius of Oak St.

Sure, the logic for the ending is a tad janky, but I needed that feel-good conclusion (along with the dog not dying either , of course). To me, the movie is only about dinosaurs on the surface. The more interesting part is the dynamic between the Platt family. At the beginning of it, Denise and Greg are clearly having some marital problems, and Denise feels resentful and stagnant with her husband. But they start to find their way back to each other while in crisis. And then she sees him take charge of their family by defending them – even though he sadly dies in the process. It’s the weird, twisted sci-fi family therapy they somehow all needed.

Sure, characters often need to die in movies, but not in this one. I love Hathaway’s anecdote about how Greg coming back to life positively affected one viewer. The ending adds a bit of wish fulfilment and helps even out the tone of the whole experience. Look, if the end is going to include two Jeannettes by the end , Greg can live too! I'm so happy he did.

articles.title: Where to Watch the NWSL Championship: Washington Spirit vs. Kansas City Current
articles.summary: Washington Spirit will have the benefit of a hometown crowd at the sold-out game, while the hungry Kansas City Current seek their first title.
articles.content:
The National Women's Soccer League final is set, with Kansas City Current traveling to Washington Spirit's Audi Field. Jeff Goldblum was honored with a tribute award at the Marrakech Film Festival on Saturday, reflecting on more than half a century in cinema during a heartfelt speech in which he thanked his many on-screen collaborators and insisted that "the stories that we tell matter."

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Avatar: Seven Havens has ended its first season without some key bending styles seen in action, and thankfully the producers behind it all teases the ones missing in action still exist in the future of the series. Avatar: Seven Havens introduced a whole new generation of the franchise with its brand new story set over two hundred years following the end of The Legend of Korr a , and that means the overall world of Bending has been changed throughout all of that time as well.

With Avatar: Seven Havens Book One coming to an end, producers Sehaj Sethi and Ethan Spaulding participated in a Reddit AMA to answer all kinds of questions fans had about the series. This included the status of whether or not Lava or Metal Bending still exists in this world that's 200 years out from its predecessor, and thankfully it's confirmed that they do and we still might get a chance to see those styles in action in future seasons .

When asked about the chances of potentially seeing Lava Bending in Avatar: Seven Havens ' future, Spaulding confirmed that "Lava Bending has never left!" with Sethi further teasing, "You gotta keep watching!" As for the current status of Metal Bending, that had been much more in question given that one fan had noted how an Earth Bender moved the Earth under a piece of metal rather than the metal itself. But Spaulding confirmed that it still exists in the world 200 years later, but it's just far more rare than seen in the other shows.

"Post Cataclysm, Metal Bending is an even more rare style, but it still survives," Spaulding revealed. This did raise a lot of questions considering how Sand Bending had beens seen in Avatar: Seven Havens , and there's still the wonder if any of the other sub-Bending categories would appear in the future . But with the producers confirming that these styles are still active even all these years in the future, it opens up the opportunity for more of that in future seasons. And that's going to happen soon enough as more episodes are already on the way.

It's not clear if these styles will appear as soon as Avatar: Seven Havens ' second season, but it's even more likely now that Pavi has left Ellora in search of the other Havens in the future . As she unlocks more of her latent chakra powers in the coming seasons, it's also possible that Pavi will be able to unlock all sorts of new sub-abilities too. Or meet others using these Bending styles. There might even more more sub-abilities that have yet to be seen that have developed after all this time.

Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2 is currently scheduled to kick off its run with Paramount+ beginning on May 21st next year with 13 episodes. They'll be streaming with Paramount+ with a few episodes being offered each week from that point, and then will be followed by the release of Season 3 (which also has another 13 episodes) later in 2027. The series will then come to an end with its fourth season sometime after. Are you curious to see these missing Bending styles in Avatar: Seven Havens ' future? Let us know all of your thoughts in the comments.

articles.content:
CAA chief Bryan Lourd is urging the full Congress to pass the No Fakes Act and deliver it to President Trump for signature, a move Lourd says would protect everyone, famous or not, from nonconsensual digital replicas of their voices and likenesses.

In a guest essay published in today's New York Times, Lourd writes, "The Senate and House should move quickly and deliver the bill to President Trump for signature. That would ensure Americans retain control of their images and voices in the A.I. era."

The No Fakes Act was approved unanimously by the Senate Judiciary Committee in June, and, Lourd contends, there "is momentum to pass it through the full Congress before the end of the year." He calles it "one of the few A.I. bills with true bipartisan support." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

Hollywood, Lourd writes, "is not afraid of new technology."

"The objection from actors, musicians and other creators is to a world in which anyone can use their face or voice without permission," he writes. "In fact, many artists are already embracing A.I. on their own terms. Some of them are making deals with companies that are creating their A.I. likenesses, with their consent."

Lourd poses the issue as not just for Hollywood. "A content creator learned on her honeymoon that a YouTube ad was using an A.I. version of her to sell erectile dysfunction supplements," he writes. "Is all this legal? Right now, it’s an open question. But it shouldn’t be."

"Hollywood doesn’t need America’s leaders to devise a new concept for new circumstances," writes the chief executive and co-chairman of Creative Artists Agency. "We need them to extend and enforce the rules that already exist. The use of Americans’ faces, voices, performances and creative works is already subject to rules at the federal or state level that say, in short: You need to get permission, and you need to pay for the use."

"This principle has guided the entertainment industry for more than a century," he continues. "Whether it can continue to protect Americans may be decided in the coming weeks. The No Fakes Act would create a federal prohibition on creating nonconsensual digital replicas of any person’s voice or likeness — famous or not." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The No Fakes Act, Lourd says, "would apply a tried-and-true formula to the A.I. era: control, consent and compensation. It would set a uniform federal standard to replace outdated, ill-fitting state laws, many of them written with an analog world in mind. Its supporters include all sides of the table: SAG-AFTRA, the union representing actors and other performers; the Motion Picture Association, representing the studios; and tech companies including IBM, Google and OpenAI."

Earlier this month, Lourd told Deadline's Dominic Patten, that the issues around AI are "about the fundamental relationship between technological progress and creative rights, and who determines the value of creative work, who decides how that work is used, and whether creators will share in the opportunities AI creates."

Now the studio is teaming up with a surprising partner to put fans in the first-person POV of a few characters. In this new Visa ad, fans step into the shoes of Thor, Gambit, Beast, and The Thing as they navigate what seems like their everyday lives—cruising the Bifrost, getting flowers, ordering hair pomade, and having their rougher edges sanded down.

While the first-person POV was a nice change of pace from the usual advertising fare , Marvel Studios partnering with seemingly random businesses to promote its newest movie isn't a new tactic; they recently teamed up with the MLB during the World Series to run a TV spot with a few crumbs of new footage —and fans weren't particularly impressed. There was also another TV spot , this one standing on its own, that added a few sprinkles of never-before-seen moments to the conversation, including Doom performing some sort of magic while Drax looks at a sky that appears to be exploding in fire, Mystique morphing into Yelena, and Shuri and M’Baku meeting with Ben Grimm in a desert landscape.

A brand new Visa commercial features characters from ‘AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY’, including Thor, Gambit, Beast and The Thing. pic.twitter.com/m8oL6SEo5g

It's no secret that fans have been less than impressed with how Marvel has handled the marketing for Doomsday up to this point. With promised teaser trailers that never seemed to arrive, recycled content that showed the same 10 seconds of footage over and over, and a constant leaning into the joke that Steve Rogers is still Captain America, it seemed like audiences were in a content drought despite being so close to the film's release . And while the new Visa ad has a fun, casual vibe to it, it's obvious that Marvel has no interest in revealing anything new about the upcoming movie.

“This is the 10th f*cking time I’ve seen Doom stopping the Stormbreaker with his fingers,” said one fan. Another added, “And we are still not getting a real trailer. Two months to go," said one fan after the MLB spot. After the standalone TV spot, another said, "'New teaser’ and it’s rewarmed nachos.” So while there's no doubt that theaters will be filled to bursting on December 18th when Avengers: Doomsday drops, there's going to continue to be grumbling about the way that the movie was marketed and how Marvel handles its film marketing in general (we can choose to collectively forget the time when the Russo Brothers were their own surprise guests and a Doom-inspired cafe).

In the case of one game, this means that rather than its normal $60 price point, it is available for just $3. All of the deals come courtesy of the Xbox Store and are only available until December 1. After this, the AAA first-person shooter series will be priced like a AAA first-person shooter series rather than a bargain-bin steal.

The first-person shooter series in question is DICE and EA's military series, Battlefield , which, after a disappointing run, finally bounced back last year with the release of Battlefield 6 , one of the best games in the long-running franchise to date. And Battlefield 6 is on sale, but not at the prices of the rest of the series. It's been discounted by 67%, though, which drops its price from $70 to $23.09. The installment right before it, meanwhile, is 95% off on the Xbox Store, which means $2.99 rather than $60. Joining it are discounts that drop Battlefield 1 to $0.99, Battlefield 5 to $1.97, and Battlefield 4 to $0.99. There are also the same 95% discounts on various special editions for each game for those who want to pay a little extra for all the add-on goodies.

Battlefield 2042 and Battlefield 4 don't have a very active player base. You can find games, but it's not the most robust active player base. The latter is simply because of age, and the former is because it is the worst Battlefield game of all time. Battlefield 5 , meanwhile, has more active players than both, and is worth checking out in 2026 if you like World War 2, in particular. The most robust player base in 2026, other than Battlefield 6, is Battlefield 1 , one of the best games in the series, and the series' most recent take on World War I .

As you would expect, these are either the lowest prices ever for these various games or match the previous lowest prices, and they are unlikely to ever get much cheaper, as there isn't much gap between 95% off and simply giving the games away for free. The only way they could really get cheaper is through price reductions to the normal MSRP. In the case of something like Battlefield 2042 , which is still $60, this will happen, but with the older games, they have already been marked down to $20, and they are unlikely to be made any cheaper than this beyond sales.

If these particular deals don't tickle your fancy, there is a metric ton available on the Xbox Store, with more to be added for Black Friday and Cyber Monday. Meanwhile, a trio of N64 games is now available for free for some Xbox Series X users .

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Star Wars made its full anime series debut with a major Star Wars: Visions spin off hitting earlier this Summer, and the creator behind it revealed how there were some surprising complications when developing the series under Lucasfilm. Star Wars: Visions Presents - The Ninth Jedi expanded on the original shorts seen in the anthology into a full series offering a whole new take on the Star Wars timeline. But while the production team had full freedom with the shorts, it turns out the situation was much different for the series.

Kenji Kamiyama, the director behind Star Wars: Visions Presents - The Ninth Jedi and many other legendary anime releases , spoke about working on the series during 2nd Aichi-Nagoya International Animation Film Festival ( as spotted by Comic Book Resources ), and explained that he came across some surprising trouble with Lucasfilm when expanding on the shorts into a full work, "At first, I was told I could make it freely, but as it became a series, unique rules suddenly came out and Lucasfilm got angry at me."

But while Kamiyama noted a difficulty working with Lucasfilm over turning the shorts into a full series, it seems that the creative process ended up working out in a way that Kamiyama had been satisfied with, "It all started when I first wanted to make Star Wars , so I was genuinely happy to be working with those people, and at the same time, I wanted to test whether what I had been doing would be accepted by the people I admired, so I'm glad that I was able to achieve that." It all seems to have worked for Disney as well.

Star Wars: Visions Presents - The Ninth Jedi released with Disney+ earlier this Summer as a limited series, but those behind the scenes have teased it would be possible to bring it back for a second season. At the very least, the spinoff has now opened the doors for potentially more of the shorts from Star Wars: Visions to get their own spinoffs in the future as well. Considering the critical success of this first outing , it's very much possible as Disney is always seeking out new Star Wars projects.

Star Wars: Visions Presents - The Ninth Jedi director Kenji Kamiyama also expressed a desire to continue the series with a potential second season . Although it was released as an eight episode limited series, the production team realized as they wrote out the episodes that there's potentially much more of the story to tell. Given how it also takes place at a far off version of the timeline, there's plenty of room to expand on the Star Wars universe lore as a whole.

Star Wars: Visions has been proof positive that Star Wars is a perfect fit for anime through the lens of all sorts of creators and their respective stories, and this new spinoff has been the strongest example of this yet. If you wanted to check it out along with the three seasons of the anthology series, you can now catch up with it all now streaming with Disney+ in the meantime. What did you think of The Ninth Jedi ? Would you want to see it return for Season 2? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: 5 Novelizations That Made Classic Comic Stories Even Better
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Titan Press Comic books are a special medium. When the medium is on full display, it can craft stories that couldn't exist anywhere else, but that doesn't mean that incredibly talented […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Comic books are a special medium. Also called graphic novels, these books combine art and words to create something new that combines the greatest elements of both and generates something truly unique. When the medium is on full display, it can craft stories that couldn't exist anywhere else, but that doesn't mean that incredibly talented people haven't tried. Occasionally, a comic book becomes so beloved that people want to dig even deeper into it than the comic allowed, so the graphic novel is adapted into a traditional novel. There's always something lost in translation, but there's also a whole lot to gain in this jump. Today, we're looking at five novelizations of Marvel and DC comics and dissecting exactly what makes them so good and, depending on who you ask, even better than the stories they were based on.

This classic five-issue miniseries was adapted into a 283-page novel, exploring Matt's childhood and transition into the man who would become Daredevil. Just like Miller's foundational work, this novel takes us through Matt's life, exploring the various influences that forged him into the man he is . From his complicated but loving relationship with his father to his passionate connection with Elektra, everything is here, but they are dove into with new depth and time. The greatest things about this novel, easily, are the additional scenes and lingering moments that focus on how each character feels and their reasoning for what they do.

In his prime, Miller was a master of saying everything he needed to about a character without digging into the emotions themselves. He had a less-is-more style that showed rather than told the important emotions, leaving that mostly to the art. When it works, it works very well, but his work tends to come off as distant because of it. This novel, however, spends pages examining how each important moment affects Matt and others. It was a treat to slow down and sit in Battlin' Jack's resentment of how his life turned out, making every moment with him hit even harder. Matt's inner struggles are so much more vivid, as this book knows exactly when restraint is necessary, as well.

This novel adapted not just the classic "Death of Superman" story, but also its two immediate follow-ups in "Funeral for a Friend" and "Reign of the Superman," detailing the Man of Steel's death and return to save the day once again. Of course, this book was also written by the legendary Roger Stern, who also helped pen the original comic this was based on. That gave him a unique perspective that elevates this book by leaps and bounds, as Stern knew exactly what to focus on. This novelization was effectively a chance to retell this story as it felt to him, not just as the comic books demanded it must be formatted.

The most obvious example is in how it began, as chapter one kicks off with Superman saving John Henry Irons, which wouldn't be revealed until much later in the comics, which aimed to keep the mystery of the four Supermen alive. It's that kind of focus that places heart at the front of this adaptation. It knows exactly what made the comic work and hones in on those moments, all while also doing an incredible job of condensing and introducing necessary comic book lore in a way that any new reader could pick this book off the shelf and understand it. This work places the heart of the story before everything else, with a clear love for the source material, and that shines through to create an adaptation that makes us live the story in a new but equally delightful way, focused on emotions instead of the novelty of Superman being dead.

The "Civil War" event is one of Marvel's events that gets looked at less favorably with each passing year, but there's no denying that the impact it had was massive , nor that it's an idea that you can't help but let ruminate around in your head. This novel understands that the premise of Captain America and Iron Man standing on opposite ends of this conflict is easily the most interesting part of this event, and it takes that in stride, spending a wonderful amount of time in each character's head. The strongest parts of this novel, easily, are when we see the motivations that drive both men and push them farther and farther apart.

This novel also fundamentally establishes that this is different from the comic, bringing both the sliding timescale and retcons into account. The events were moved up to the year the book was released, setting it during Barack Obama's presidency instead of George W. Bush's, and even depicting Spider-Man post "One More Day" changes, meaning that he never married Mary Jane. It's a wonderful look into what "Civil War" would have looked like to the heroes at that time. I'll admit some bias for it, at least, given that I flipped through a few pages while I was a kid, and the description of Spider-Man's battle against Iron Man as Tony chased him into the sewers has stuck with me ever since.

"Days of Future Past" is one of the X-Men's most important storylines, and despite the fact that it's just two issues long, it was adapted into a 254-page novel. The obvious question is where all of that extra content came from, and it emerged from a combination of exploring everything added to the original story after the fact and taking it in its own direction. "Days of Future Past" has a truly inordinate number of sequels, and this novel draws most directly on the expanded history Rachel Summers wouldn't get till far after the original comic. Her perspective, absent from the comic, adds interesting contrast and context, but the biggest change is the inclusion of Kitty Pryde waking up in her older body.

In the comic, Kitty was simply replaced by her older self, but the novel had them switch places. Chapters alternated between Kate trying to guide her friends towards stopping the apocalypse, and Kitty living a waking nightmare where the world she was still learning how to save was falling apart. The added perspective gives the story a ton of extra content to explore, and the jump between characterizations is wonderful. Kate and Colossus's conversation before she travels to the past was especially wonderful, with even the add-ons capturing Peter's voice perfectly.

Just as with The Death and Life of Superman , this iconic Batman story was adapted by one of the many minds behind it, Greg Rucka. Of course, this is a special case, as this is the one novelization that actually cut far more content than it added. "No Man's Land" was a year-long status quo change that was told across a hundred issues, and no single novel could cover everything and do them all justice. Instead, this adaptation glossed over most of the day-by-day activities, instead honing in on the largest emotional beats, such as Hutnress's development, while replacing what it removed with dives into the characters the original focused too little on.

The big winners here are Renee Montoya, Cassandra Cain, and Harley Quinn. Renee's dynamic with Two-Face is explored and built like nowhere else here, serving as a fantastic dive into both of their psyches. It also gave extra context to Harley's introduction to the comics, given that this is where she hopped over from the cartoon. My personal favorite was definitely the extra attention given to Cass before her debut in the comics . Most of "No Man's Land" seems to lead up to her debut, but she wasn't seen until two issues before she became Batgirl. This novel takes the time to explore who she is, what she did, and how she fits into Gotham.

I could honestly go on about this novel all day. It doesn't have the scale that makes the original comic so captivating and addictive, but it knows exactly what emotional beats need to build towards the fantastic moments that made the comic work. The opening chapters told from Barbara's perspective are downright beautiful, and I was on the edge of my seat, even though I knew everything that was coming. I definitely recommend checking this out if you get the chance.

Which novelization of a comic do you think captures the spirit of the original the most? Let us know your personal favorite in the comments below!

Points were made. As awesome as it would have been to see Maysilee kill a Gamemaker with one of her poisoned darts, that sequence also complicated her relationship with Haymitch shortly before her death. Instead, Francis Lawrence and company decided to keep the District 12 tributes as a united force until Mckenna Grace's character was killed by bird mutts. articles.title: Why Bari Weiss’ CBS News Is Going Through More Staff Shakeups Months After 60 Minutes Firings
articles.summary: More changes are coming to CBS News.
articles.content:
Over a year into her tenure as CBS News’ Editor-in-Chief, Bari Weiss has sought to move the storied organization into a new era. Those attempts have apparently come with some growing pains, however, as the network has seen staffing changes and fluctuating ratings in recent months. At the same time, drama has been swirling around Weiss due to her reported vision for the brand and editorial decisions she’s made. Now, the company is experiencing more major staffing shakeups months after those 60 Minutes exits .

In the aftermath of the Paramount Skydance/Warner Bros. Discovery merger, the media conglomerate Skydance has been born, and further consolidation is on the horizon. The new company recently offered buyouts to employees at CBS News, and dozens of employees reportedly accepted the deals. Status (via The Daily Beast ) reports that different departments within the Eye Network’s news branch were impacted, including CBS Evening News , CBS Mornings , 60 Minutes and the company’s news bureaus.

A source spoke out about this major development, saying “It’s pretty much an extinction-level event.” That particular insider was apparently from the London bureau, which has reportedly been hit the hardest by the buyouts. As for the cause of this, it’s said that London-based employees had been displeased with Foreign Editor Shayndi Raice since she allegedly called out staffers for “insubordination.” Concerns about CBS News being merged with (the recently acquired) CNN are also said to have factored into these staff exits.

What’s also notable about this situation is that it comes on the heels of a significant development regarding CBS News’ Face the Nation . Senior executive producer Mary Hager is leaving the show and the network after having worked there for 35 years. (It’s unclear whether Hager’s departure has to do with her accepting a buyout.) Additionally, executive producer Anne Hsu is leaving as well for a new gig with the network’s Hong Kong bureau. So Weiss now finds herself in the position to reshape the show after allegedly having considered firing host Margaret Brennan earlier this year.

Weiss and 60 Minutes executive producer Nick Bilton made some major changes to the news magazine show on May 28, 2026 (which is allegedly known as “Black Thursday” within the company). On that day, the company officially parted ways with veteran correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega as well as EP Tanya Simon and others for reasons that have still yet to be specified. And, shortly after that, another seasoned correspondent – Scott Pelley – was fired after a heated meeting with Bilton. It was during that conversation that Pelley allegedly accused Weiss of “murdering” the show .

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball first made its debut with Shueisha's Weekly Shonen Jump magazine 42 long years ago, and the legendary series is still the biggest action icon in all of anime and manga after all this time. Dragon Ball wasn't the first notable series that Toriyama made an impact with, but its inarguably the most notable project that Toriyama had ever produced. That's even more the case all these decades later as the franchise is still inspiring new releases coming out to this very day .

Dragon Ball first made its debut with Shonen Jump on November 20, 2984 in Japan, and through the over four decade stint of the franchise it's become one of the most successful action anime and manga franchises of all time . It might have been a rather humble manga story that originally began with a young boy with a tail seeking out a group of magical wish granting items, but it has since exploded into a multiverse with god level fighters, multiple timelines, iconic transformations and more.

Dragon Ball introduced fans to a young boy with a monkey tail named Goku. Upon meeting a teen girl named Bulma searching for magical wish granting items known as the Dragon Balls, Goku had set out on an adventure that ended up being much bigger than fans could have ever expected at the time. It started out on a much smaller scope as Goku's journey was more mystical at first. That was until he turned into a Giant Ape at the end of his first major adventure dealing with Emperor Pilaf. It turned into an entirely different series from there.

While Goku had an inkling for martial arts thanks to time spent with his grandfather Gohan, the series started to take on more of an action shape for the adventures moving forward. World tournaments, demons, rival fighters, assassins, androids and more began to appear, and it changed the world forever. Dragon Ball was never really the same as much like Goku continued to evolve in power and skill , the series around him began to change as well to encompass even bigger adventures and more thrilling battles. Almost as it to reflect Goku's aging into adulthood.

Dragon Ball first really made waves in the United States with the second major iteration of the franchise. Known as Dragon Ball Z outside of Japan, this was the next major entry of Akira Toriyama's story that really opened up the world from there. Taking matters out into space, it was revealed that Goku was actually from an alien race known as the Saiyans and had family members he had no idea about . But little did fans know at the time, Goku would eventually ascend into godhood by the time all of his stories would come to their end decades later.

As Dragon Ball continues to commemorate its 40th anniversary, fans are now seeing new projects make their way to screens such as the Dragon Ball Super: Beerus remake anime series, and brand new anime series Dragon Ball Super: The Galactic Patrol. Though Toriyama had initially ended Goku's story following the Majin Buu arc, he would later return to introduce Gods, Angels, and even a full blown multiverse with Dragon Ball Super thereafter . And that's really only scratching the surface of it all.

Akira Toriyama sadly passed away back in 2024, but the franchise has continued to go on in his absence. New releases such as Dragon Ball Daima were able to take his final ideas for the story and reveal a whole new adventure even after his death, and the Dragon Ball Super manga will hopefully be able to return to cap off its own story someday instead of being locked into its current hiatus . Regardless at what shape the future takes for the Dragon Ball franchise from here on out, it's clear that it's still going strong either way.

Dragon Ball is a rare franchise that has gone on for so many decades that its various iterations have introduced different generations of fans to different takes on Goku over the years. It's been to such an extent that there's a version of Goku available to fans of many different ages, and it's sported a legacy that will continue to break through its limits for many more decades to come .

How do you feel about Dragon Ball' s legacy after 42 years later? What are some of your favorite moments over its tenure? What do you want to see from the future of it all? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.
